ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. goes
   C. went
   D. going

3. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

4. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Language School.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Language School.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.

5. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.

6. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.

7. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.

8. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.

9. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

10. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. quickly
   C. blue
   D. happiness

11. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only an action

12. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. No full stops

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Attentive listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Language Welcome and and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Language School and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Pre Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

1. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.

2. C — went

3. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

7. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

9. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

10. A — run

11. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

12. A — One main idea with supporting sentences
